title: add-representative-workload-runners-and-reporting-pipeline-for-benchmark-lab
author: Ava Patel
description: Context and motivation: This PR adds a set of representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and a lightweight reporting pipeline for the Benchmark Lab. The goal is to standardize how we capture end-to-end latency/throughput profiles across models and hardware configurations and to provide a reproducible pipeline that publishes summarized metrics to our metrics store and a static report bucket. This work is driven by ENG-4172 and follow-ups from recent perf canary runs where we lacked comparable workload runners across families. Changes in this PR: 1) new representative workload runners: a small runner framework under benchmark-lab/workload-runners that includes chat, zero-shot completion, and embedding workloads with configurable sequence length distributions and batching parameters; 2) profiling baselines: scripts and baseline artifacts for p50/p95 latency and token/sec for representative model+hardware pairs (gpt-medium-fp16 on rtx-a5000, llama2-13b-int8 on a100), plus a recorder to capture KV cache behavior; 3) reporting pipeline: a lightweight pipeline that ingests workload runner output, computes summarized metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, failure-rate), writes metrics to the internal metrics topic and uploads a small HTML+JSON report to the benchmark-lab reports bucket; 4) CI and infra: a GitHub Actions workflow to run a smoke set of workload runners on PRs and a scheduled nightly job that runs the full suite against a cheaper spot pool; 5) docs: README, quickstart, and example Linear tasks for running local and remote runs. Design decisions and rationale: The runners are intentionally small and configuration-driven to allow reuse between hosted and dedicated capacity tests. Profiling captures both per-request latency and internal runtime counters (kv-cache hits, batching efficiency) so we can attribute regressions to scheduling vs model runtime. The reporting pipeline is decoupled: runners emit line-delimited JSON artifacts; a separate collector runs aggregation and publishing to minimize test flakiness. Checklist: - [x] Add workload runner framework and three canonical workload configs - [x] Add baseline artifacts and scripts to record profiling traces - [x] Implement reporting aggregator and upload path - [x] Add GitHub Actions smoke test workflow - [x] Update README and quickstart - [x] Add Linear tasks and docs examples to assist recurring runs Commit summary: commit 1: add benchmark-lab workload runner framework and configs; commit 2: add profiling scripts and baseline artifacts; commit 3: add reporting aggregator and S3/GS upload support; commit 4: add GH Actions smoke workflow and nightly schedule; commit 5: docs and README updates. Files changed (high level): - benchmark-lab/workload-runners/{runner.py,configs/*.yaml} - benchmark-lab/profiling/{record_baseline.py,kv_recorder.py,baselines/*} - benchmark-lab/reporting/{aggregator.py,report_generator.py,templates/report.html} - .github/workflows/benchmark-smoke.yml and benchmark-nightly.yml - benchmark-lab/README.md and quickstart.md Testing performed: Local smoke runs against a small CPU fallback were executed in CI to validate end-to-end flow. Nightly scheduled runs executed in our staging spot pool and uploaded reports to a staging reports bucket. A subset of runs were executed on dedicated capacity to validate KV cache logging. CI summary: initial run failed due to missing environment variables in the action; author updated workflow to use repo-level secrets and reran; final CI passed all smoke tests (lint, unit tests, smoke-run). Performance verification: The new baseline artifacts were compared against previous informal runs; p95 regressions were within expected variance for the tested models. Observability and dashboards: The PR includes a Grafana dashboard JSON template to visualize p50/p95 token/sec over time and a set of recommended alerts for regression >10% p95 or >5% failure rate. Backwards compatibility and rollout: No breaking API changes. The runners are opt-in and do not affect existing benchmarks. The reporting pipeline uses a new metrics topic and a new reports bucket scoped to benchmark-lab. Deployment and operational notes: Nightly jobs are scheduled in GitHub Actions and can be migrated to the perf-canary cluster in a follow-up. Cost controls include running a reduced sample on spot instances and a configurable max-run-time. Review conversation snapshot: - Diego: please add tests to assert the aggregator handles partial inputs and corrupted lines. - Author (Ava): added tests and a small retry/backoff in aggregator, pushed fix in commit 3. - Linnea: can we add a knob to disable KV capture to avoid extra memory on smaller runners? - Author: added config toggle and documented memory implications. - Marcus: approved after the smoke CI passed and tests were added. Merge outcome: Squash and merge into main on 2026-02-25 after CI green and approvals. Release notes: - Added representative workload runners and profiling baselines for Benchmark Lab. - Added reporting pipeline that publishes aggregated metrics and static reports. - Added scheduled nightly runs and CI smoke tests. Notes for SRE and infra: update the metrics topic retention if necessary and ensure report bucket lifecycle policy is set to 90 days for staging and 365 days for prod. Related PRs: pr-18123-benchmark-lab-reporting-pipeline-v5.json and pr-2142-add-benchmark-runners-reporting-pipeline.json. Contact and follow-ups: Follow-up work tracked in ENG-4191 for unified canary integration and ENG-4203 for expanding model coverage.
